answer: Trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, limiting how far endorsements travel in one round. For a sybil cluster with low conductance φ, only a small fraction of stationary trust flow crosses its sparse external cut per step. With capped per-node weight and votes tied to reachable trusted mass, this bounds aggregate voting power by boundary support, not internal account count—even if accounts are named ocean, hollow, or cedar.
